comparable_cases.why_comparable: Same parcel (2015 Chestnut St, part of 2015-2027 Chestnut), same NC-2 zoning, restaurant continuation. This is a 2021 DPH health referral for the existing Pacific Catch restaurant use at the subject address, 0 meters away.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 14 days for continuation of the existing restaurant use at this exact location. Since this is not a change of use but an enlargement within the same parcel that already operates as Pacific Catch, the Planning Department treated it as a continuation requiring only agency sign-off, not a Commission hearing.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 3347 Fillmore St (14 meters away, same NC-2 zoning), approved 2021 for continued non-formula retail restaurant use. Shows the distinction Planning makes between formula and non-formula retail in NC-2.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 7 days. Planning explicitly noted this was a 'non-formula retail restaurant' permitted under Section 711. The fast approval contrasts with formula retail cases that require CUA hearings, underscoring that formula retail status is the deciding factor for whether an NC-2 restaurant goes to a hearing or gets staff sign-off.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant with full bar (ABC Type 47) at 3318 Fillmore St (74 meters, NC-3 zoning), approved 2021. While in NC-3 rather than NC-2, shows how Planning handles alcohol licenses in nearby Neighborhood Commercial districts without triggering CUA for the alcohol itself.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 12 days. ABC Type 47 (full bar) was approved as accessory to a restaurant use in the NC-3 district without a CUA. In NC-2 and NC-3 districts, alcohol service incidental to a bona fide eating place does not require conditional use authorization; only bars (non-restaurant) and certain entertainment uses trigger CUA.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant with accessory billiard parlor permit at 94 meters in NC-3 zoning, approved 2022. Shows Planning's treatment of accessory entertainment devices within restaurant uses as permitted without CUA.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 6 days. Entertainment Commission billiard parlor permit (pool table and mechanical bull) approved as accessory to existing non-formula retail restaurant in NC-3 without requiring conditional use. Demonstrates that accessory entertainment in a restaurant context is treated permissively in Neighborhood Commercial districts.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant with ABC Type 41 at 3340 Steiner St (95 meters, NC-2 zoning), approved 2021. Same zoning district and alcohol license type as the existing Pacific Catch operation.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 14 days. Type 41 beer-and-wine license approved in conjunction with a first-story restaurant in NC-2 under Section 711. Confirms that alcohol licenses accessory to restaurants in NC-2 are routinely approved at staff level without hearings, provided the business operates as a bona fide eating place.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 3318 Fillmore St (74 meters, NC-3 zoning), ABC Type 41 approval in 2020, showing rapid turnaround for alcohol referrals in the immediate neighborhood.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 5 days. Type 41 license approved as accessory to a restaurant use in NC-3 under Sections 712 and 102. The 5-day turnaround illustrates that ABC referrals for existing restaurant operations are among the fastest Planning approvals when the use is already permitted.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 2120 Greenwich St (176 meters, Union Street NCD zoning), approved 2022 for ABC Types 47 and 58 (full bar and caterer). Shows how Planning treats off-premises catering and alcohol as accessory uses to an existing non-formula restaurant.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 21 days. Type 47 full bar and Type 58 caterer permits approved as continuation of existing non-formula retail restaurant use, with the caterer permit treated as an accessory minor use for off-site food sales. Demonstrates Planning's flexibility with accessory uses when the primary restaurant use is established.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited restaurant at 2101 Lombard St (112 meters, NC-3 zoning), approved 2020. Shows how Planning treats limited-service restaurants (similar to the subject's limited cooking profile) in nearby Neighborhood Commercial districts.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 8 days. Limited restaurant use permitted in NC-3 as non-formula retail under Sections 102 and 712 without superseding any prior building permit conditions or Commission motions. Confirms that limited-service restaurants are treated as permitted uses in Neighborhood Commercial districts without additional scrutiny.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited restaurant at 2095 Chestnut St (93 meters, same NC-2 zoning), approved 2019. Another limited-service restaurant on the same street, showing consistent approval patterns for this use type.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 25 days for a limited restaurant in NC-2. The similar limited-cooking profile and NC-2 location make this a strong analog for the subject's approval pathway, assuming non-formula retail status. Planning treated it as a health department referral with straightforward staff-level approval.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 3347 Fillmore St (14 meters, same NC-2 zoning), ABC Type 41 approved in 2017. Same location as other referrals, showing repeat approvals for the same property over multiple years.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 3 days. Type 41 license permitted in conjunction with continued restaurant use in NC-2 under Sections 711.44 and 790.91, with the requirement to operate as a bona fide eating place. The 3-day turnaround is among the fastest on record for this corridor.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm formula retail status in writing with San Francisco Planning Department.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a pre-application meeting or zoning counter confirmation: Does Pacific Catch (11 other locations per the profile) meet the Section 303.1 definition of formula retail? Explain that the business is enlarging an existing restaurant within the same parcel that has operated as Pacific Catch since 2003. Ask whether a Conditional Use Authorization is required or whether the enlargement can proceed as a continuation under Section 711 with agency referrals only.

filing_playbook.action: Register for a San Francisco Business Registration Certificate and a California Seller's Permit.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector (fee is tiered by gross receipts, starting at $55 plus $4 state fee); the registration year runs April 1 to March 31. Register for the seller's permit at the CDTFA website the same week (free, often issued same day). Every other city permit asks for the Business Account Number (BAN), so complete this step before filing building or health permits.

filing_playbook.action: Hire a California-licensed architect to prepare tenant-improvement plans for the building permit, including the change-of-occupancy analysis.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Engage an architect with San Francisco restaurant experience to prepare stamped plans showing the merged storefronts, kitchen layout, restrooms, ADA upgrades, and occupancy calculations. Request a code analysis that identifies the existing occupancy group (likely A-2 or B) and confirms whether the project triggers a change of occupancy. Route the DPH plan check and the building permit application together to avoid bouncing between departments.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain workers' compensation insurance, register for EDD payroll taxes, enroll employees in food handler card training, and certify one food safety manager.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Quote workers' comp through a broker or State Fund before the first employee is hired (mandatory from day one). Register online with EDD e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying wages (free). Enroll all food-handling employees in an ANSI-accredited food handler card course ($7–$15, valid 3 years) within 30 days of hire. At least one owner or employee must pass an accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe or equivalent, ~$125–$200, valid 5 years) before the DPH final inspection.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost are for approval of the Conditional Use Authorization and health permit to operate, assuming formula retail status is confirmed and a CUA hearing is required. The CUA typically takes 120–300 days from application to final approval (including pre-application meeting, environmental review, Commission hearing, and 30-day appeal period); the health permit plan check and permit to operate add 35–105 days in parallel with the building permit. Government fees: CUA application ~$3,100 (adjusted annually for CPI; was $2,747 in 2023–24), building permit $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation, DPH plan check $828–$2,500 (new restaurant is typically $2,207 for 8 hours), health permit to operate $470 application plus $0 annual license for restaurants in FY2026–27, business registration $55–$700 tiered by gross receipts, and sign permit $300–$1,500. If Pacific Catch is determined to be non-formula retail, the CUA is not required and the timeline drops to 14–120 days (building permit plus health permit in parallel), with government fees of ~$1,500–$18,500. The figures above do not include architectural, legal, or construction costs, which are not government fees.

records_summary: 2027 Chestnut St is in the NC-2 zoning district where a restaurant use is principally permitted on the first story. The site has operated as Pacific Catch restaurant since 2003 with an active Type 41 ABC license (beer and wine). The parcel encompasses 2015-2027 Chestnut St, with multiple restaurant tenants over the years. The immediate block is heavily saturated: 16 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft and 16 registered food/drink businesses within 500 ft, signaling high density. Over the last 10 years only 4 dated use decisions were found within 1,000 ft (too few for a meaningful approval rate), though all 4 were approved.
